# v0.4.0 — Every credential in OpenBao; every privileged action through one door

**Upgrading from 0.3.55:** follow [Upgrading to 0.4.0](https://github.com/thatsme/AlexClaw/blob/main/docs/deployment/upgrade-0.4.0.md) — the backup to take first, OpenBao's first start, what the first start of 0.4.0 moves, how to confirm it, what to do after, and how to roll back. It is the one procedure; these notes do not restate it. Two lists belong here, because they name what 0.4.0 removed.

**Action after upgrading: set the gateway owners, or the bots answer nothing.** `telegram.owner_user_id` and `discord.owner_user_id` start blank; set them on the Config page (see "Gateways" below).

**Every dynamic skill is checked again at the first start.** One that fails containment — an `import`, a call outside the contained set, a removed permission, or a web fetch through `SkillAPI` without `def external, do: true` — is not loaded, and the log names it and the calls. The guide's "After the upgrade" says what a skill must declare.

**Delete from `.env`** — no longer read, and they hold live credentials in plain text. The values in use are the ones in the database, which the upgrade moves:

| Variable | Now |
|---|---|
| `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` | `telegram.bot_token` on the Config page |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `llm.gemini_api_key`, `llm.anthropic_api_key` on the Config page |
| `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GOOGLE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN` | `google.oauth.client_secret` on the Config page; the refresh token from the authorization flow |
| `WEB_AUTOMATOR_TOKEN` | generated at the first start by `automator-token-init`; nothing to set |
| `OLD_SECRET_KEY_BASE` | not needed: changing `SECRET_KEY_BASE` re-encrypts nothing; the key-rotation release commands are gone |

**Removed, for dynamic skills and chat:** the SkillAPI functions `create_workflow`, `add_workflow_step`, `run_workflow`, `write_skill`, `read_skill`, `load_skill`, `unload_skill` and `reload_skill`; the permissions `skill_write`, `skill_manage` and `workflow_manage` (a skill that declares one is not loaded); `import` in a dynamic skill (`import Logger`, `import AlexClaw.Skills.Helpers`, `import SweetXml`); MCP skill tools and `mcp.tool_timeout_ms`; the chat commands `/events`, `/google auth` and `/automations`, and `--tier` saving a default. `/record`, `/replay`, `/automate`, `/connect`, `/disconnect`, `/setup 2fa`, `/confirm 2fa`, `/disable 2fa`, `/shell`, `/coder` and `/skill` answer where it is done in the admin UI.

## Changes

### Secrets

- OpenBao 2.6.3 (pinned by digest) runs as its own service on an internal network shared with AlexClaw only, with TLS, raft storage, a file audit device, automatic unseal from the host key file, a non-root user and a read-only root filesystem. `openbao-init` makes the certificate and, once, initialises it.
- A credential is typed into the form of what uses it — the Config page, a step, a resource, a recording's login, an LLM provider — and the save stores it in OpenBao, bound to the host (or origin) it is sent to. The record keeps a reference. There is no separate secrets page.
- A secret setting shows when it was set, never its value or part of it. An empty input keeps the value; a new one replaces it; Clear deletes it from OpenBao.
- A value with surrounding whitespace or a control character is refused on entry.
- Credentials are attached when a request is sent, for the host it goes to. A request carrying one is not followed across a redirect to another host. A recorded login is typed only while the page is on its origin.
- Every value resolved from OpenBao appears as `[secret]` in step results, run history, gateway messages, audit rows and logs.
- Workflow exports show a credential as `<secret not exported>`; importing empties it, to be entered again. Run definitions show `<secret>`.
- Deleting a step, workflow, resource or setting deletes its secrets; duplicating a workflow copies them.
- The Gemini key is sent in the `x-goog-api-key` header, no longer in the URL.
- `api_request` logs a request's scheme, host, port and path, never the query string.
- Nothing is encrypted under `SECRET_KEY_BASE` any more; it signs sessions. The encrypted-column machinery and its release commands are removed.
- When OpenBao is sealed or unreachable, AlexClaw keeps running and login still works; steps that need a credential fail, and the log says what failed.

### The one door

- Every privileged action — control-plane writes, secrets, identity, data, runs, recordings — is a named action performed by one module, which decides per entry point (admin UI, chat, MCP, skill, webhook, cluster, system) whether it is allowed and what proof it needs, and audits every attempt, allowed or refused.
- Every admin UI change needs the elevation. Database download, data export and workflow export now need it too (a 403 otherwise); clearing run history is gated; loading a skill needs a code.
- Login, logout, every run start and each secret catalogue change write an audit row. A change that is undone still leaves its refusal row.
- Sign out everywhere also ends every elevation.

### Second factor and login

- The authenticator key lives in OpenBao's TOTP engine, which checks codes; AlexClaw stores no part of it. The last accepted code is refused for 90 seconds.
- While OpenBao cannot answer, an authenticator code is answered as unavailable and not counted against the code-entry locks; a recovery code is still accepted in the browser.
- Recovery codes are drawn from the cryptographic generator and kept as OpenBao HMACs.
- 2FA is set up, confirmed and turned off on the Services page only, with an authenticator code or a recovery code. Setup is refused while 2FA is on; cancelling a setup never removes an active key. Turning 2FA off discards the recovery codes.
- With the authenticator and every recovery code lost, `make reset-2fa`, run on the host, turns the second factor off; nothing in the application can. See [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/thatsme/AlexClaw/blob/main/SECURITY.md), "If everything is lost".
- The admin password is kept as a PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 hash (600,000 iterations), locally, so login works while OpenBao is sealed. A new hash ends every login made under the old one. A hash row that cannot be read refuses every login rather than falling back to `ADMIN_PASSWORD`.

### Skills and containment

- Containment is checked for every dynamic skill at every load and every boot, whatever approved it. A code approves the permissions a skill declares, never calls outside the contained set; the permission cap applies to unattended (generated) loads.
- The approval screen lists a skill's permissions and flags the risky ones and pairings (knowledge or memory writes read back into prompts, `skill_invoke`, a private read beside `web_read`).
- The contained set admits typespecs, string interpolation, `System.monotonic_time`, `Process.sleep`, `Exception.message`, `:crypto.hash`, and `Path`'s name functions only (`join`, `basename`, `dirname`, `extname`, `rootname`, `split`, `relative`, `relative_to`, `type`). `SweetXml` is no longer admitted.
- New `SkillAPI` functions: `parallel_map/4` (bounded, ordered, under the calling skill's authorisation), `module_docs/2`, `parse_xml/2` (refuses a document type or entity declaration; returns plain maps), and `http_request`'s `:secret_headers`.
- The external-call check resolves aliases, as containment does: a skill that fetches through `SkillAPI.http_get`, `http_post` or `http_request`, aliased or written in full, declares `def external, do: true`, and its output is sanitised.
- A `SkillAPI` call is checked against the skill actually running, never the module it names. A skill's availability check runs as that skill.
- Every skill runs through one executor, which checks availability first: a step whose skill is unavailable fails with the skill's reason, and none of its code runs.
- The reasoning loop runs its skills through the one door, audited.

### Gateways

- Telegram and Discord answer only the owner user in the owner chat (`telegram.owner_user_id` in `telegram.chat_id`, `discord.owner_user_id` in `discord.channel_id`), all set in the admin UI. **Action:** after upgrading, set the owner user ids, or the bots answer nothing.
- Chat commands operate, they do not author: settings, credentials, 2FA, recordings, skill generation and shell commands are admin-UI only.
- The Telegram bot token is read from OpenBao once, and again when it is rotated or Telegram answers 401; the Discord bot token is read at start and handed to the Discord client again when it is rotated. A 401 on a `telegram_notify` step's own token no longer invalidates the main token.
- Google is connected and disconnected on the Services page; the OAuth callback needs the session that started it.

### Workflows

- A step of `shell`, `coder`, `db_backup` or `web_automation` runs only in a run the scheduler starts, or one started from the admin UI with a code; the Workflows and Scheduler pages ask for the code.
- A chat's `/run` of a workflow with such a step is answered at once, naming the step and where it can run.
- The GitHub webhook starts its configured workflow through the one door, audited; a disabled or protected workflow is refused.
- Cluster: another node's request runs an unprotected workflow only; the sender is taken from the connection, and the node must be registered and named in the gate's `allowed_nodes`. An empty `allowed_nodes` allows no one. A workflow gated by `receive_from_workflow` no longer runs locally: it runs only when an allowed node triggers it.

### Backup, restore and export

- OpenBao is backed up with `make backup-openbao REASON=<reason>`: a raft snapshot taken by the on-demand `openbao-backup` service (compose profile `backup`) with a snapshot-only AppRole whose single-use token is bound to that service's address. AlexClaw never mounts its credentials and cannot take a snapshot of its own vault. Snapshots go to `~/backups` or `OPENBAO_BACKUP_DIR`, never to `BACKUP_DIR`; each is checked before success is reported. The unseal key and the recovery key are not in the snapshot.

- An export no longer carries, and a restore keeps, this installation's admin password hash, second factor, recovery codes, secret catalogue, authorisation policies, login protection (`auth.rate_limit.*`, `auth.trust_proxy_headers`) and gateway owners. An older file's copies are skipped, and the result says what was kept.
- A restore refuses a file in which a step or resource references a secret this installation does not hold, and a file holding values 0.3.x encrypted (restore it into 0.3.55 and upgrade).
- After a restore every other admin session is signed out, and the settings and policies are read again.

### MCP

- MCP reads and runs enabled, unprotected workflows. It has no skill tools and writes nothing.
- The MCP key is generated on the Config page and shown once; only its HMAC is stored. Every read applies one redaction rule per kind of data.

## Security

The security model of this release — what OpenBao holds and how AlexClaw reaches it, the one door and its policy, the second factor, containment, the gateway owners, restore, and the known limitations — is described in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/thatsme/AlexClaw/blob/main/SECURITY.md), notably "Secrets in OpenBao", "Control-Plane Elevation", "Two-Factor Authentication", "Dynamic Skill Loading", "Telegram Gateway Security", "Inter-Node Authentication (Clustering)" and "Known Limitations and Design Decisions". The OpenBao deployment and its operator procedures are in [docs/architecture/openbao.md](https://github.com/thatsme/AlexClaw/blob/main/docs/architecture/openbao.md).
